class.name: NNHTNBinding
class.brief_description: Binds a method argument to each value of a world state collection in turn.
class.description: Used in [member NNHTNMethod.bindings]. While planning, a binding reads the [Array] at [member state_key] from the predicted world state and offers each entry, or each entry's [member entry_field], as the argument [member variable]. Every value is a separate alternative: when it fails, or anything planned after it fails, the search retries with the next value. [codeblock] var binding := NNHTNBinding.new() binding.state_key = "coins" binding.variable = "target" binding.entry_field = "node" binding.order = NNHTNBinding.NEAREST binding.origin_key = "agent_position" method.bindings.append(binding) [/codeblock] Values are ordered by [member order]; ties keep source order. [member conditions] then filter them, and at most [member NNHTNSearchSettings.max_binding_candidates] values that pass are used. When more pass than the cap allows, the search is incomplete: an empty result is reported as [constant NNHTNRoot.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED] instead of [constant NNHTNRoot.NO_PLAN]. Values are deep-copied per alternative, while [Object] values keep their identity. Entries whose bound value is a freed [Object], or a [Node] queued for deletion, are skipped silently. Entries without the field the binding needs are reported and skipped. A [member state_key] that does not hold an [Array], or a [constant NEAREST] origin that is not a [Vector3], is reported and offers no values. [member state_key], the [member origin_key] of a [constant NEAREST] binding, and the keys read by [member conditions] are replanning triggers.

method.name: get_validation_errors
method.description: Returns one message per configuration problem: an empty [member state_key] or [member variable], an [member entry_field] with an empty segment, an invalid [member order], a missing or malformed [member origin_key] and [member position_field] for [constant NEAREST], a missing or malformed [member order_field] for [constant NUMERIC_FIELD], and empty or unparseable [member conditions]. Empty when the binding is valid. A method with an invalid binding is skipped by planning with an error, and shows these problems as configuration warnings.

members.member: Filters every value must pass. They are evaluated like [member NNHTNNodes.conditions], against the predicted world state, with [code]args[/code] holding the method's arguments plus this binding's [member variable], so [code]args.target.score > 2[/code] filters on the bound value. They can read the variables of earlier bindings, but not of later ones.
Reverses [member order]: [constant SOURCE] runs from the last entry to the first, and the sorted orders run from the largest key down. Ties still keep source order.

An optional dot-separated path read from each entry, which must then be a [Dictionary]. The value at that path is bound instead of the whole entry, while [member position_field] and [member order_field] can still read other fields of the entry. Uses the same syntax as [member NNHTNArgumentReference.field_path].
How the values are ordered before they are tried.
For [constant NUMERIC_FIELD], the dot-separated path of the [int] or [float] sort key, read from the entry and, when the entry has no such field, from the bound value. Ignored by the other orders.
For [constant NEAREST], the world state key holding the [Vector3] distances are measured from. Ignored by the other orders.

For [constant NEAREST], the dot-separated path of each entry's [Vector3] position. When the entry has no such field, the bound value is used if it is a [Vector3] or a [Node3D] (its [member Node3D.position]), then the entry itself if it is a [Vector3]. Ignored by the other orders.
The world state key holding the [Array] of entries. Must not be empty.
The method argument that receives each value. Must not be empty. A later binding with the same variable overrides the earlier value.

constants.constant: Keeps the order of the source [Array].
Orders by squared distance from the [Vector3] at [member origin_key] to each entry's position (see [member position_field]), closest first.
Orders by the number at [member order_field], smallest first.
